$comment: SHARED BACKEND<->FRONTEND CONTRACT. Every error_kind that can reach the
frontend on a `tool_error` SSE frame, and what the UI must do with it.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. ChatPanel's subset test proves every kind in
TOOL_ERROR_BANNER_KINDS has KIND_COPY — a kind that routes losing its
copy. It cannot see the other direction: a kind that SHOULD route and
does not. That is the direction that actually bit us, twice, and both
times the symptom was identical and silent — the banner's copy existed
and was simply unreachable, so the user got a truncated gray tool line.
`inactive_acting_user` was corrected that way, and so were
`not_authorized` and `unknown_profile_id`.
Neither side can close it alone: the backend knows what it can emit and
nothing about copy; the frontend knows its copy and cannot enumerate the
backend. So the set lives here, and both sides assert against it.
HOW IT IS ENFORCED.
backend/tests/test_tool_error_kind_manifest.py
derives the set from the source and fails if it differs from the
keys below. A NEW error_kind therefore fails the build until
somebody classifies it here.
frontend/src/components/ChatPanel.manifest.test.tsx
asserts every `banner` kind is in TOOL_ERROR_BANNER_KINDS AND in
KIND_COPY, and every `inline` kind is in neither.
THE DERIVED SET IS A SUPERSET, deliberately. It is every `error_kind`
literal yielded at a `tool_error` site, plus every one appearing in ANY
dict literal anywhere in the backend, because tool dispatch forwards any
exception carrying `detail['error_kind']` (chat_service._run_one_tool's
except block) and those details are not always written inline at the
raise — `study_in_flight` is built in `project_context.study_swap_refusal`
and raised as a variable, which an HTTPException-scoped scan missed.
Some kinds it finds are only ever raised from a route and never from a
tool handler; those are classified `inline` with that as the reason.
Over-including costs a line of JSON; under-including is the bug this file
exists to prevent.
surface: 'banner' = promote to the error banner (needs KIND_COPY).
'inline' = leave as the gray tool line.
Changing one is a UI decision. Write down why, as the entries do.

flow_project_not_open.why: get_project_flow was asked about a project that is not the open one: the flow is read from the loaded network. The detail names the project; the assistant opens it (activate_project) or says it must be opened first. There is no conversation-wide recovery action.

invalid_reference.why: resolve_reference refused a malformed request (unknown target or component class, a blank or oversized name or run_id, or no class to resolve against). The per-call detail says which; the assistant asks for the missing piece instead of guessing. There is no conversation-wide recovery action.

invalid_result_views.why: list_result_views refused a malformed request (exclude_shown that is not true or false). The per-call detail says which; the assistant retries with a valid flag. There is no conversation-wide recovery action.

schema_field_too_large.why: get_component_schema refused one field whose complete descriptor exceeds the bounded metadata page. The per-call detail names that field; the assistant reports incomplete discovery rather than clipping it or claiming a complete schema. There is no conversation-wide recovery action.

restriction_unavailable.why: Saved personal project restrictions could not be read at tool admission or worker pickup. Fail closed and direct the user to refresh Access and approvals; never silently assume standard rules.

user_restriction.why: The authenticated user saved a personal read-only project rule. The non-read tool did not run; inspect or change the rule explicitly in Access and approvals, without weakening server confirmation floors.

aborted.why: The user pressed stop. Announcing their own action in a banner is noise.

approval_unavailable.why: The approval of a confirmed (or policy auto-approved) action could not be written to the approval log, so the action did not run: approvals fail closed (chat harness issue 18). Usually the app-data directory is full or not writable.

baseline_has_no_case.why: Decision study (S5): the investment case was asked for the grid-only baseline, which every case is measured against. Route-only today; a client-side slip, nothing for the user to fix.

capability_unsupported.why: The profile cannot do what the turn needs (vision, tools). A configuration problem only the user can fix, and the turn is over. It already had KIND_COPY and did not route — the same unreachable-copy shape as inactive_acting_user.

commercial_binding_invalid.why: The commercial config cannot bind to this network (a missing Link, an unrated snapshot, ...). The model reads the message and fixes the config within the turn.

commercial_config_invalid.why: define_participants: the stored commercial config no longer validates. The model re-saves it with update_solver_config first.

confirmation_denied.why: The user denied the card. Their own decision, already visible on the card.

confirmation_revoked.why: The card was withdrawn because the conversation's scope changed (durable_conversation.rebind_scope); the action did not happen. Recorded as approval/decided revoked (chat harness issue 18).

confirmation_expired.why: The card timed out; the action did not happen and the user must redo it.

descendants_exist.why: A destructive project operation was refused. The user chooses cascade or rename.

discussed_run_required.why: export_run_evidence (or a follow-up) needs a discussed or named run_id. The model calls discuss_project_run or list_project_runs within the turn.

empty_file.why: Upload rejected. The user must supply a different file.

excel_parse_failed.why: One read failed on one workbook. The turn continues and the model reports it in prose.

file_integrity_error.why: Raised by upload_service on a stored-file checksum mismatch, reached through the upload ROUTE rather than a tool handler. Kept here because the forwarder would carry it if a tool ever did.

file_too_large.why: Upload rejected against the 25 MB cap. The user must act.

finance_inputs_invalid.why: The stored finance inputs do not validate (the route's 422 lists the errors). The model tells the user which fields; they are corrected in the Investment tab.

finance_inputs_missing.why: run_investment_case / solve_ppa_price with no stored finance inputs. The model asks the user to fill in the Investment tab; there is no chat tool that writes them.

eh_report_not_found.why: export_eh_report_docx found no stored Energy Hub report. Per-call; the message names the remedy (run_eh_study first) and the model relays it.

figure_not_found.why: Raised only by GET /{name}/reports/{id}/figures/{figure_id}, the report viewer's source, for an unknown or malformed figure id. No tool serves figure bytes, so it never reaches a tool_error frame.

fork_changed_since_run.why: Decision study (S5): an option fork's network changed after the run (opened, edited or re-solved outside the study), so its case would price one network with another's bills. Route-only today; the message tells the user to re-run the study.

fork_has_children.why: Decision study (S4): deleting a study, or re-running it, refused because a user branched a project from one of its option forks. Route-only today (routers/studies.py); the user moves or deletes that project and retries, so the refusal reads in place rather than as a banner.

fork_solving.why: Decision study (S4): a study fork still has an active solve-queue job, so it cannot be removed yet. Route-only today; transient, the user waits for or aborts the job.

format_not_supported.why: One tool could not read one format. Per-call, and the model can try another route.

image_analysis_timeout.why: The vision call timed out at 30 s. Nothing came back and the user should retry.

image_too_large.why: Attachment rejected against the 10 MB multimodal cap.

import_tariff_ref_conflict.why: The project's inline tariff differs from the Library item its ref names. The model explains and asks which to keep; a binding code surfaced by attach_tariff.

goal_already_set.why: set_goal while the session already has a goal (chat harness issue 17). The model's own slip, answered in the tool result: complete the goal first; only the user resumes or stops one, from the goal strip.

inactive_acting_user.why: The account stopped being active mid-turn. Nothing will work until it is fixed, and a gray tool line truncates that away — this is the correction the whole manifest generalises.

inline_tariff_would_be_replaced.why: attach_tariff refused to replace a project's inline import tariff with a different Library tariff. The model asks the user and calls again with replace_inline=true — a question it is already asking in prose.

intake_changed_since_run.why: Decision study (S7 gate): the study's answers (site, load, tariff, PV) changed after the run, so its findings, cases and report would describe options built from other answers. Route-only today; the message tells the user to re-run the study.

internal_error.why: An unhandled server failure. It reaches the client on a turn-terminal `error` frame, which the banner renders directly from KIND_COPY — it is not yielded at any `tool_error` site.

invalid_goal.why: set_goal with an empty or over-long objective or max_rounds outside 1-20 (issue 17). The model corrects its own call; nothing for the user to fix.

interrupted.why: The session event log's synthetic closer for a tool call the process died during (chat harness issue 13), written when the log is read back for repair. It goes to the log and to the model's history, never on a live tool_error frame.

invalid_base64.why: Malformed payload into one tool call. The model can correct and retry.

invalid_decision.why: A confirm request carried something other than approve/deny — a client bug, not a user-actionable state.

invalid_discussed_run.why: discuss_project_run / set_discussed_run received a malformed run_id or open_ui flag. The model corrects arguments within the turn.

invalid_filename.why: Upload rejected on the filename. The user must rename.

invalid_png.why: One image failed to decode in one tool call.

invalid_mapping_plan.why: PUT /{name}/reports/{id}/template/plan (or set_report_mapping) received a body that is not a mapping plan, or a plan that needs sanitising under strict mode; the detail carries the sanitiser's notes naming the heading or section that does not exist. Per-call: the model (or the plan editor) corrects the plan within the turn, as with invalid_tool_args.

invalid_run_evidence.why: Run-evidence validation or a path-containment guard refused this evidence operation. Its own error explains the refusal; the turn can continue without a conversation-wide banner.

invalid_report_id.why: A report id that is not 16 lowercase hex characters, refused at the store boundary before any path is joined. Route-only in WP1; when WP6's report tools pass a model-typed id, the model sees the message and corrects within the turn, as with invalid_tool_args.

invalid_tool_args.why: The model sent arguments that do not match the schema. It sees the error and retries within the turn; a banner would fire on a self-correcting step.

invalid_transcript.why: Raised by POST /chat/import validating a pasted transcript. Route-only — no tool imports transcripts.

investment_case_busy.why: run_investment_case / solve_ppa_price: a solve or a study is running (the study mesh's 409). A standing condition the model reports; the user waits for it or aborts it.

investment_case_not_solved.why: run_investment_case / solve_ppa_price before a solve (or on a stale dispatch). The model says the network must be solved first; the run needs the solved dispatch.

investment_case_refused.why: solve_ppa_price: the finance adapter refused to build the case (FinanceRefused; its `code` says why, e.g. template_not_annual). The model explains the code in prose; get_investment_case shows the same refusal for a run.

investment_case_request_invalid.why: An investment-case tool got an argument out of range (an empty owner, a page < 1, a target IRR or year outside the SolvePpa bounds). The model corrects the argument and retries, like invalid_tool_args.

currency_mismatch.why: A value in one currency would replace a value priced in another (an EUR Library reference on an asset priced from a non-EUR regional pack). Nothing is converted; the model explains and leaves the value as it is.

reference_target_unsupported.why: apply_library_reference named a class the reference does not price (wind/PV apply to a Generator, an electrolyser to a Link; a StorageUnit is not supported). The model names the right asset or explains.

reference_confirmation_needed.why: apply_library_reference needs the user's explicit confirmation (`missing`: dc_ac, grid_connection or money_year, each with its text). The model asks the user and calls again with confirm naming only what they confirmed.

library_reference_unknown.why: get_library_reference named a technology/projection year the shipped references do not hold, or passed component without asset. The model re-reads list_library_references and retries; a route code surfaced by the Library references route.

library_ref_stale.why: A Library reference no longer matches its item (edited or removed). The model re-reads the Library and retries or asks; a route code surfaced by attach_tariff.

ledger_changed_since_run.why: Decision study (S5): the assumptions ledger was edited after the run, so the solved options no longer match it. Route-only today; the message tells the user to re-run the study.

load_not_found.why: The named load is not in the network. The user gave a name that does not exist.

mime_not_allowlisted_for_multimodal.why: The file type cannot be attached; the user is told to use the read tool instead.

missing_api_key.why: The active LLM profile has no key in its slot. The chat turn reports it on its own error frame; the report generation routes (WP3) are the first to emit it as a tool_error literal. ChatPanel already routes this kind to the key-entry banner (TOOL_ERROR_BANNER_KINDS, KIND_COPY with the user.env field), so the classification must say banner or the frontend contract test fails.

no_acting_user.why: No authenticated identity is bound to the turn, so every project-scoped tool 401s. Same family as inactive_acting_user and equally terminal — it was the one member of that family still unrouted.

no_active_project.why: Most tools need a project; the model recovers by asking which one, in prose, inside the same turn. Promoting it would banner a question the assistant is already asking.

no_chat_session.why: A session-bound control tool (discuss_project_run, use_toolset, start/resume_task) ran without an active ChatSession. The turn framework normally supplies one; when it does not, the model reports the refusal and does not invent session state.

no_active_workflow.why: advance_workflow was called with no workflow started on the session. The model reads the message and calls start_workflow within the turn (chat harness issue 06).

no_commercial_config.why: attach_tariff needs a commercial config with a poc_link first. The model sets it (update_solver_config) and retries within the turn.

no_evidence.why: POST /{name}/reports/generate found no Energy Hub reference design, no reliability surface and no worksheet rows: there is nothing a model may narrate. The evidence-only POST still produces a document that states every section as not established; generation refuses. The message names the remedy (run a study) and the model relays it.

no_template.why: A mapping plan was proposed or stored (POST/PUT …/template/plan, propose_report_mapping, set_report_mapping) for a report that has no template bound. The message names the remedy (bind one with set_report_template) and the model relays it within the turn.

no_goal.why: pause_goal or complete_goal with no goal set (issue 17). A harmless model slip; the strip already shows there is none.

not_authorized.why: The account may not take this action (e.g. switching the instance-wide profile). Terminal for the request and needs an administrator.

option_not_solved.why: Decision study (S5): the last run did not solve the option, or the study does not own its fork. Route-only today; the option list already shows which options solved.

option_unknown.why: Decision study (S5): the question has no such option id. Route-only today; a client-side slip, not a condition the user must act on.

parallel_destructive_not_allowed.why: Several destructive calls arrived in one turn and none ran. The user must reissue them one at a time.

pdf_conversion_failed.why: POST …/reports/{id}/export {format: pdf}: LibreOffice exited non-zero or wrote no file; the message carries the head of its stderr. Inline: the assistant relays the reason and offers the .docx, which rendered fine — the conversion is the only thing that failed.

pdf_not_available.why: POST …/reports/{id}/export {format: pdf} on a host without LibreOffice (soffice/libreoffice not on PATH): a capability, not a failure. Inline: the assistant offers the .docx instead; the viewer hides the PDF button from GET capabilities and never sends this.

profile_switch_requires_new_chat.why: The session is bound to one provider's block shapes, so a mid-session switch is refused. Emitted as an `error` frame with its own `new-chat` action; the banner already gets it without tool_error routing.

project_exists.why: A save was refused to avoid an overwrite. The user chooses rename or force.

project_lock_not_held.why: Raised by routers/projects.py when a mutation arrives without the lock — a client-sequencing bug rather than a user-actionable state.

project_lock_unavailable.why: Someone else holds the lock. Transient and usually resolves; the model reports it and can retry.

project_locked.why: Raised by the projects and solve-queue routes. Route-only today; kept classified so it cannot arrive unnoticed if a tool starts reaching it.

project_switched_mid_turn.why: DELIBERATE, and do not 'fix' it: the same guard also yields this as an `error` frame (chat_service, right after the per-tool refusals), and THAT is what reaches the banner. Promoting the tool_error copy too would show the banner twice for one event.

rate_limited_local.why: The local per-session turn limiter, raised by the chat route before a turn starts — so it never arrives on a tool_error frame in practice.

report_job_in_flight.why: POST /{name}/reports/generate (or a section regenerate) while a report job is still running — one job per process; the message says to wait or abort. Route-only in WP3; WP6's generate_report tool relays the message and the model waits or aborts within the turn.

report_job_not_found.why: POST /{name}/reports/generate/abort when no report generation has ever run in this session. Nothing to abort; the model relays it.

report_mode_not_supported.why: POST /{name}/reports was asked for a mode this build does not offer (only evidence_only until WP3's generator lands). Route-only in phase 1; when WP6's report tool passes a model-typed mode, the message names the supported one and the model corrects within the turn, as with invalid_tool_args.

report_not_found.why: No such study report (or version of it) in this project. Per-call; the message names the remedy (generate one first) and the model relays it, exactly as eh_report_not_found is handled.

report_section_not_found.why: A section id the report does not have, on generate (`sections`), on the per-section regenerate (WP3) or on get_report(section_id) (WP6). The message names the id; when WP6's tool passes a model-typed id the model corrects within the turn, as with invalid_tool_args.

result_unavailable.why: read_result was given a locator that has expired, belongs to another chat or user, or was read during a checked answer. The model reads the message and re-runs a narrower query instead (chat harness issue 16).

report_table_not_found.why: get_report_table (WP6) was asked for a table id the report version does not carry. Tool-only: the routes serve whole documents. The message lists the ids the report has, so the model corrects within the turn, as with invalid_tool_args.

report_version_not_found.why: GET …/reports/{id}/versions/{a}/diff/{b}: one of the two versions does not exist. Inline: the tool result names the remedy (list_reports shows latest_version); the model corrects the argument.

roundtrip_not_a_report.why: POST …/reports/{id}/roundtrip: the file carries no sec:<id> bookmark and no heading that names a section of the report, so there is nothing to merge and nothing was written. Inline: the assistant tells the user which report the copy must come from.

roundtrip_unreadable.why: POST …/reports/{id}/roundtrip: the uploaded file is not a Word document the reader can open. Inline: the tool result names the file and the remedy (export again, edit in Word, upload the .docx); the assistant relays it.

sdk_not_installed.why: The SDK the active profile's wire needs is missing from this build, surfaced as a 400 by the report generation routes (WP3); the chat turn reports it on its own error frame. Per-call; the message says so and the model relays it.

session_not_yours.why: Raised by the chat STREAM route when the caller-supplied session_id belongs to another user — sibling of unknown_session, and route-only for the same reason: the refusal happens before a turn starts, so it cannot arrive on a tool_error frame. Not a banner because the client already recovers from it without asking the user to do anything: api/chat.ts carries the error_kind onto the Error and ChatPanel calls startNewChat(), because a legitimate user can meet this through no fault of their own and must not be left retrying an id the server will refuse forever. Since CH-6, GET /history hands each user only their OWN session, so the remaining route here is a transcript written before turns recorded their author.

site_connection_invalid.why: set_site_connection: a two-way meter Link, one Link named as both import and export, an unknown timezone, or a refusal of the kept commercial config that has no kind of its own (its `code` names it, e.g. fca_needs_saved_project; commercial_binding_invalid, library_ref_stale and solver_in_flight keep their own kinds). The model explains and asks for the right Link or zone within the turn.

site_connection_link_missing.why: set_site_connection named a Link that is not in the network; the message lists the likely candidates. The model picks one with the user and retries.

site_connection_wrong_direction.why: set_site_connection: the PoC Link runs into the grid, or the export Link does not run from the site side to the grid. The model names the Link that runs the other way and retries.

report_never_assembled.why: Decision study (S7): reading or rendering the decision report (JSON, HTML, DOCX, XLSX) before it was ever assembled. A client-side sequencing slip on a route-only surface; the message says to POST the report first.

report_prose_invalid.why: Decision study (S7): the report's prose guard refused a paragraph (a number outside a fact reference, or an unresolved reference), naming the section and paragraph. The templates are the product's own, so this is a defect to fix, not a condition the user acts on; route-only today.

snapshot_count_mismatch.why: Supplied rows do not match the network's snapshots. The data must be corrected.

snapshot_range_mismatch.why: Supplied time range does not match the network's snapshots.

solve_ppa_ambiguous_contract.why: solve_ppa_price without contract_id on a case with several PPAs. The model asks which contract, then retries with contract_id.

solve_ppa_cash_not_established.why: solve_ppa_price: the post-tax equity cash is not established even at a zero price (a missing input). The model points to get_investment_case's reasons.

solve_ppa_contract_not_found.why: solve_ppa_price: no owner-sold PPA settlement line matches contract_id (or the case has none). The model names the contracts it knows or asks which one — within the turn.

solve_ppa_needs_redispatch.why: solve_ppa_price on a contract that changes the dispatch: a finance-only solve cannot re-dispatch (plan C9). The model explains the limit in prose.

solve_ppa_irr_ambiguous.why: solve_ppa_price: a price makes the NPV zero at the target, but the truncated equity cash has several IRRs and the engine's own (the root closest to 0) is not the target, so the price does not give the target IRR as reported (P4 gate). Its `code` carries that IRR; the model explains, nothing to fix in the UI.

solve_ppa_no_root.why: solve_ppa_price: no price in the search range reaches the target (its `code` says why, e.g. the target is met at a zero price). A finding the model reports, not a failure to route.

solve_ppa_not_linear.why: solve_ppa_price on a contract whose settlement is not linear in its price (plan C9). An answer the model explains; there is nothing for the user to fix in the UI.

solve_ppa_not_owner_sold.why: solve_ppa_price on a contract the owner buys, not sells (plan C9). The model explains that only an owner-sold PPA can be solved.

solve_ppa_price_unknown.why: solve_ppa_price on a contract whose price is not established in the case. The model says the contract needs a price first.

report_failed.why: Recorded on a published run-evidence manifest when a report job ends failed; get_run_evidence surfaces the typed error field.

solver_failed.why: Recorded on a published run-evidence manifest when a foreground solve ends failed; not a user-facing tool_error banner — get_run_evidence surfaces the typed error field.

study_failed.why: Recorded on a published run-evidence manifest when an adequacy/study worker ends failed; get_run_evidence surfaces the typed error field.

solver_in_flight.why: A foreground solve is running and the operation was refused. The user waits or aborts.

study_in_flight.why: An adequacy study is running and a save/queue was refused. Deliberately QUIET on the client (`QUIET_TOAST_CODES` in api/client.ts): it is a standing condition the caller handles, and one toast per autosave tick would bury the workbench.

tax_pack_not_found.why: The finance inputs name a tax pack with no version covering the financial close. The model reports it and asks for another pack or date — a question in prose.

template_refused.why: define_participants: the template cannot be built for this site (its code says why, e.g. template_needs_group_contract). The model tells the user or picks another template.

tagged_render_error.why: POST …/reports/{id}/export (export_report_docx) with a TAGGED template whose tag the document cannot fill (an unknown field, table or figure id, or a Jinja syntax error); the message quotes the paragraph and lists the known names. Per-call: the user fixes the template or binds another, and the model relays the message rather than retrying.

template_not_a_template.why: set_report_template / POST …/template (or generate_report with template_file_id) named an upload that is neither of kind report_template nor a .docx by MIME. The message names the file and the remedy (upload a .docx with ?kind=report_template); the model corrects the file id within the turn, as with invalid_tool_args.

template_not_untagged.why: A mapping plan was proposed or stored for a TAGGED template, which fills its own tags and needs no plan. Per-call; the message says so and the model relays it (export_report_docx is the next step).

template_unreadable.why: The bound template's bytes could not be opened as a Word document (docx_reader.TemplateReadError: a renamed zip, a truncated file) on bind, GET, plan or export. The message names the reason; the user must supply a real .docx, and the model relays it rather than retrying.

study_never_run.why: Decision study (S4): asking for the run status or aborting a study that has never been run. A client-side sequencing slip, not a condition the user must act on.

study_report_format_invalid.why: Decision study chat tool (U3): generate_study_report was asked for a format other than docx, xlsx or html. The model's slip; it reads the message and asks again.

study_request_too_large.why: Decision study (F1 B2): a /studies request body over the size limit (the 25 MB load-file cap plus headroom), refused 413 by services/study/body_limit.py before it is parsed. Route-only, no chat tool posts a study body; the message tells the user to use a smaller file.

study_running.why: Decision study (S4): a second run, a delete, or another study refused while a study runs on the base project. Reaches chat through the study tools (U3); the message names the study and the user waits or aborts it.

study_stage_invalid.why: Decision study chat tool (U3): run_decision_study was asked for a stage other than options or tornado. The model's slip; it reads the message and asks again.

time_column_parse_error.why: The time column could not be parsed as datetimes; the user must fix the input.

too_many_multimodal_blocks.why: More than 20 attachments. The user must send fewer.

tool_call_cap_exceeded.why: The turn hit MAX_TOOL_CALLS_PER_TURN and stopped. Terminal, and the only per-turn bound there is.

task_step_limit.why: A bounded task (the card explanation, budget.task_cap) reached its tool-call or round limit; the over-limit tools were not run and the turn stopped with the plain message. The user asks to continue in a new turn. Inline until the card explanation's header entry (H2b) gives it copy.

tool_error.why: The forwarder's own fallback when a tool raises something with no structured error_kind. Generic by construction — there is no copy to write, which is exactly why the specific kinds beside it exist.

tool_not_offered.why: The endpoint asked for a tool that was never offered this turn. On a branch whose point is aiming the assistant at arbitrary endpoints, the user should see it.

tool_not_started.why: The shared chat-tool pool had no free worker, so the call was cancelled before it ran. Inline for the same reason as tool_timeout -- the turn continues and the model can retry or route around it -- and distinct from it because nothing exceeded a deadline: the remedy is capacity, not a smaller request.

tool_timeout.why: One tool exceeded its budget. The turn continues and the model can route around it.

tornado_never_run.why: Decision study (S6): asking for the fixed-size tornado's progress, or aborting it, before it was ever run. A client-side sequencing slip on a route-only surface, not a condition the user must act on.

turn_already_in_flight.why: A second turn arrived while one was running. Route-level, on an `error` frame, and the composer state already says so.

duplicate.why: Shared utterance admission (issue 02): the same utterance_id was already seen. Emitted on an `error` frame before the turn starts; the composer can show the refusal inline.

queued.why: Shared utterance admission (issue 02): a turn lease is held and this utterance became the single pending correction. Not a second turn.

stale_generation.why: Shared utterance admission (issue 02): the client generation no longer matches the coordinator after rebind/restart.

rejected_empty.why: Shared utterance admission (issue 02): blank utterance text with admission fields set. Nothing reached the model.

unknown_confirmation_token.why: A confirm arrived for a token this session does not know — a stale tab or a double-submit, not a user-actionable state.

unknown_library_kind.why: A Library tool got a kind other than tariff / contract / connection_agreement. The model corrects the argument and retries, like invalid_tool_args.

unknown_profile_id.why: The selected profile no longer exists — fires for every open chat the moment a super-admin deletes one, and C-4 made it reachable.

unknown_session.why: Raised by the chat route for a session id it does not hold. Route-only; a turn cannot be running under a session that does not exist.

unknown_decision.why: The confirmation gate got a decision outside approve/deny/expired/aborted/revoked. Defensive: /confirm only accepts approve or deny, so this should not arrive; the action did not run, and the approval log records it as unavailable (chat harness issue 18).

unknown_skill.why: use_skill named a skill that is not in the registry (harness/skills or the install's <app data>/skills), or one marked model_invocable: false. The model reads the message (it lists nothing; the catalogue is in its instructions) and corrects within the turn (chat harness issues 05 and 14).

unknown_step_kind.why: An internal script/step vocabulary mismatch — a bug in the caller, not a user-actionable state, and never yielded at a tool_error site.

unknown_tool.why: The model named a tool that does not exist. It sees the error and corrects within the turn, like invalid_tool_args.

unknown_workflow.why: start_workflow named a workflow that is not active in harness/workflows. The message lists the active ids; the model corrects within the turn (chat harness issue 06).

unknown_workflow_step.why: advance_workflow named a step the active workflow does not have. The message lists the steps; the model corrects within the turn (chat harness issue 06).

unsupported_mime.why: Upload rejected on type. The user must supply something else.

unsupported_upload_kind.why: POST or GET /{name}/uploads with a ?kind= that is not one a client may ask for (user_upload or report_template on upload; any known kind on list). Route-only today (no tool passes a kind); classified so a typo in a client cannot silently file a template as a plain upload or list nothing. The message lists the accepted kinds.

upload_not_found.why: A referenced upload is gone. The user must re-attach.

upload_quota_exceeded.why: The per-project upload quota is full. The user must delete something.

urdb_invalid.why: The URDB import arguments did not validate (e.g. valid_from not a date). The model corrects and retries.

urdb_multiple_rates.why: The uploaded OpenEI response holds several rates; the error lists them and the model retries with item_index, asking the user which one if unclear.

urdb_refused.why: A URDB import refused fields by name (the route's 422). The model lists them and asks whether to import partially (accept_partial) — a question in prose, within the turn.

urdb_upload_unreadable.why: The uploaded file is not a URDB rate the importer can read (not JSON, no rates, a REopt scenario with only a label). The model says so in prose and asks for another file.

user_code_disabled.why: Raised by routers/simulation._gate_user_code on the solver-config ROUTE, never from a tool handler, so it cannot reach a tool_error frame. Listed because the derivation matches every error_kind dict literal on purpose (it under-approximated once and missed study_in_flight). Refuses extra_functionality_code when the operator has not set PYPSA_GUI_ALLOW_USER_CODE; the settings form shows the detail where the user typed the code.

user_code_forbidden.why: Same route and same reason as user_code_disabled: a config-PUT refusal, not a tool frame. Refuses a non-admin setting extra_functionality_code, which is exec()-ed in-process. Inline so the message lands next to the field; a banner would announce another user's lack of privilege in the chat surface, which is not where the attempt happened.

validation_error.why: The forwarder's Pydantic fallback. Its message is the useful part; the kind itself says only 'the arguments were wrong', which the model retries.

value_column_parse_error.why: The value column holds non-numeric data; the user must fix the input.

value_flows_changed.why: define_participants: the value-flow config changed between its read and its write (If-Match). The model reads it again and retries.

value_flows_invalid.why: define_participants: the value-flow config names a party, asset or item the project does not have (the problems are listed). The model corrects the config and retries.

value_flows_would_be_replaced.why: define_participants refused to replace (or clear) an existing, different value-flow config. The model asks the user and calls again with replace=true.

vision_call_failed.why: The vision sub-call failed outright. Nothing came back.

vision_invalid_json.why: The vision response did not parse. Nothing usable came back.

artifact_evidence_unavailable.why: The requested artifact could not pass data/render/byte integrity checks; the file operation is refused with its own actionable message.

assurance_context_changed.why: The checked turn lost its project binding before publication, so the answer cannot safely appear for the currently selected project.

assurance_context_persistence_failed.why: The prior checked conversation checkpoint could not be durably revoked. The turn or parent control stops before execution or changing generation; retry when storage is available.

wrong_replica.why: The chat or durable parent is pinned to another application worker. Admission refuses this worker before execution and returns the owning replica identity.

assurance_publication_failed.why: The owned answer or public stream could not be committed and verified; no checked answer is available for the turn.

assurance_unavailable.why: The requested checked-answer mode is not available on this server; the turn cannot proceed under its requested publication policy.

invalid_assurance_request.why: Admission rejects a malformed checked-answer option payload before model/tool execution; this REST refusal is not a tool completion failure.

invalid_navigation.why: The navigation tool named an invalid application panel or tab; the specific tool fails without changing the active view.

invalid_progress_cursor.why: GET /api/chat/{id}/progress refuses a negative cursor query; route-only, never a tool completion failure.

invalid_component_name.why: A create, rename or import named a component with control, format or line-separator characters, an empty name, or one over 256 characters (OPEN-ITEMS item 8). Refused before anything changes; the message says which character, so the agent can pick another name.

task_checkpoint_failed.why: Durable task progress could not be saved, so the user must inspect task state before retrying any potentially effectful operation.

ui_ack_mismatch.why: The acknowledgement endpoint refuses an unissued or mismatched view acknowledgement; no completed-view assertion is created.

unsupported_assurance_version.why: Admission rejects an unsupported checked-answer protocol version before model/tool execution; the client must use a supported version.

mcp_unavailable.why: An external MCP server (chat harness issue 19) did not start, went away, or no longer lists the tool. The turn continues and the model can say the external tool is unavailable; the admin fixes the server list.

mcp_timeout.why: An external MCP tool did not answer within the per-tool budget; the request was cancelled on the server. Like tool_timeout, the model can route around it.

mcp_tool_error.why: An external MCP tool answered isError. Its own message, fenced, goes back to the model, which can correct its arguments or tell the user.

mcp_protocol_error.why: An external MCP server answered with a JSON-RPC error or a malformed reply. A server-side fault the model can only report; no UI copy would help.

invalid_source_gap_followup.why: Source-gap admission refuses a malformed or unchecked follow-up before provider work. It reaches the chat through a REST refusal or terminal error frame, rendered directly with KIND_COPY, never through a tool_error frame.

source_gap_changed.why: The native source-gap admission helper refuses a stale revision or view digest. The turn loop catches this private refusal and emits source_gap_followup_unavailable; this helper kind never reaches tool_error.

source_gap_followup_unavailable.why: The native follow-up stops before provider work when its owned origin or exact scope is unavailable. Its terminal error frame already renders the prepare-again banner through KIND_COPY; no tool completion failed.

source_gap_unavailable.why: The native source-gap admission helper cannot find the owned historical origin. The turn loop normalizes this private refusal to source_gap_followup_unavailable, so it is not a tool_error surface.

activity_project_required.why: The read-only Activity view needs an authorized saved project; its own empty/error state explains the missing scope.

activity_resnapshot_required.why: The Activity snapshot cursor expired or changed; its observer reloads authority without replaying work or approvals.

experiment_reconciliation_stale.why: The confirmation referenced an older owned receipt. Its failed tool line tells the user to inspect and confirm current proof; no project action is replayed.

experiment_reconciliation_unavailable.why: The historical submission lacks the new fenced proof. The failed tool line keeps its reservation unresolved; no fabricated no-effect verdict or retry is offered.

experiment_worker_running.why: The owned submission still holds its native fence. The failed tool line explains waiting; no result, reconciliation or retry has occurred.

invalid_experiment_comparison.why: The comparison requires two distinct owned plan IDs. The failed tool line requests a valid selection without exposing foreign sources.

experiment_comparison_changed.why: The inspected comparison no longer matches current owned sources. The failed export line requests fresh inspection; no old report or calculation is substituted.

cds_credential.why: A renewable-profile generation asked for the ERA5/atlite source without usable CDS credentials. The detail says which setup step is missing; the renewable-profile workflow coaches the CDS account, licence and key setup in words. No conversation-wide action: the synthetic source still works.

component_not_found.why: apply_generated_profile named a generator that is not on the open network (renamed or deleted since generation). The detail names it; the assistant lists the generators and asks which one, per call.

profile_bound_conflict.why: apply_generated_profile would put a generator's p_max_pu below its p_min_pu at some snapshot, which makes the LP infeasible. The detail names the generator and the first such snapshot; the assistant tells the user which bound to change, per call.

unsupported_target.why: A profile apply named a (component type, attribute) the apply path cannot write. The detail lists the supported targets; the assistant picks one or says the series cannot be applied there, per call.

unknown_family.why: A profile apply carried a profile family nobody registered (a hand-made or corrupted artifact). The detail lists the families; the assistant regenerates the profile, per call.

family_target_mismatch.why: A profile apply would write a target its family may not (a renewable capacity factor onto a load, a load shape onto a generator bound). The detail names what the family applies to; the assistant picks a fitting component, per call.

invalid_series_unit.why: A profile apply's unit does not fit its target (a price not in currency/MWh, a per-unit shape whose peak or mean is not 1, a missing scale or price basis). The detail says which; the assistant fixes the parameters and retries, per call.

dc_load_owned.why: A profile apply would overwrite the data-centre load a project's dc_load spec owns (a data-centre archetype, or a profile on the template's it_load/cooling split). The detail says to change the dc_load spec instead; the assistant points there, per call.

unknown_load.why: Load-profile generation named a load that is not on the open network, or a measured load upload has no column naming one. The detail lists the loads; the assistant asks which one, per call.

project_not_open.why: A profile was generated or uploaded for a project that is not the open one (the foreground holds another). The detail names both; the assistant opens the project first or asks, per call.

unknown_archetype.why: Load-profile generation named an archetype or preset that does not exist. The detail lists the available ones; the assistant picks one, per call.

invalid_archetype_params.why: A load archetype's parameters are missing, unknown or out of range (no peak_mw or annual_mwh, a misspelt key, a bad timezone or holiday). The detail names the parameter; the assistant fixes it and retries, per call.

load_upload_format.why: A measured load upload is not a readable timestamp + numeric load table (unreadable timestamps, a non-number, a negative reading, repeated wall-clock hours, a step coarser than an hour). The detail names the column or row; the user fixes the file, per call.

load_upload_unit.why: A measured load upload names no unit, an unknown one, or a header unit that disagrees with the stated one. The detail names the column; the assistant asks for the unit, per call.

load_upload_coverage.why: A measured load upload does not cover one full calendar year, covers several without one named, or holds a gap longer than a week. The detail says which; the assistant asks for the year or a complete file, per call.

carrier_mismatch.why: Availability generation named a wind or solar generator, whose weather profile the series would overwrite. The detail names them; the assistant picks another generator, per call.

forced_outages_not_written.why: Availability generation asked for forced outages, which the reliability study samples from each asset's own outage rate and repair time and are never written into the dispatch. The detail says so; the assistant points the user to the reliability study, per call.

unknown_availability_kind.why: Availability generation named a kind that does not exist. The detail lists maintenance, must_run and derating; the assistant picks one, per call.

invalid_availability_params.why: An availability kind's parameters are missing, unknown or out of range (a malformed window, a share outside [0, 1], a bad rule). The detail names the parameter; the assistant fixes it and retries, per call.

maintenance_year.why: A dated maintenance window does not fall in the year it would apply to, or the network is multi-period. The detail says so; the assistant uses MM-DD windows or the network's year, per call.

unknown_component.why: Profile generation named a component (link, storage unit, generator) that is not on the open network. The detail names it; the assistant asks which one, per call.

poc_tariff.why: A price series was aimed at a point-of-connection link, whose energy price the tariff in the commercial configuration sets. The detail says so; the assistant points to the tariff, per call.

cop_ambient_unknown.why: An air-source heat-pump COP was asked for on a project with no data-centre load spec and no ambient stated, so there is no site temperature to draw it from (never a default). The detail names both remedies; the assistant asks for the site's ambient or uses a ground source, per call.

cop_bus.why: A heat-pump COP was aimed at a link whose bus0 is not electricity, so it would scale the wrong input. The detail names the bus; the assistant picks the right link, per call.

two_way_floor.why: A must-run floor was aimed at a two-way link, where it would forbid reverse flow. The detail says so; the assistant picks another link or a shutdown instead, per call.

poc_bound.why: A must-run floor was aimed at a point-of-connection link, which is the grid connection, not a process. The detail says so; the assistant picks the process link, per call.

part_load_not_a_series.why: A part-load efficiency curve was asked for as a series; it depends on the dispatch, which the linear model cannot take as a time series. The detail says so; the assistant explains, per call.

unknown_series_kind.why: Series generation named a kind that does not exist. The detail lists the kinds (tou, inflow, cop, and market and part_load, which are refused with their reasons); the assistant picks one, per call.

market_bundles_unavailable.why: A market price series was asked for, but market price bundles (package C2) are not available yet. The detail suggests a time-of-use price or an upload; the assistant offers those, per call.

invalid_series_params.why: A series kind's parameters are missing, unknown or out of range (an unpriced hour, a malformed period, a bad COP temperature). The detail names the parameter; the assistant fixes it and retries, per call.

invalid_refine_op.why: A refinement op is unknown, malformed, or makes no sense for the series' target (rescale_energy on a price, keep_energy, a bad window). The detail names the op and its index; the assistant fixes it, per call.

window_clock_unknown.why: A refinement window was asked for on a series whose site clock is unknown (no project timezone, no profile timezone). The detail says so; the assistant asks the user to set the project's timezone, per call.

refine_replay.why: A recorded refinement no longer fits the regenerated series (a changed target, an op that cannot run). The detail names the op and its index; the assistant re-proposes the refinement, per call.

no_current_series.why: A refinement of the current series was asked for, but the component has none for that attribute, or carries one over several investment periods. The detail says which; the assistant offers to generate or upload one, per call.

current_changed_since_refinement.why: A series made from the component's current one was applied after that current series changed (another apply, an upload, an undo). The detail says so; the assistant refines the current series again, per call.

series_upload.why: A measured file for one field does not fit it: no column named after the component, an hour of the model missing, a value that is not a number or outside the field's range (a percentage for a share). The detail says what to change; the editor shows it in place, per call.

window_source_gap.why: A series made from a snapshot window's current series meets an hour outside that window (the snapshots changed since). The detail names the hour; the assistant refines the current series again, per call.

window_source_op.why: A shift or smoothing was asked for on a series read from a snapshot window, which knows no hours outside it. The detail names the op; the assistant uses a window scale, floor, cap or peak/energy target instead, per call.

annual_energy_on_window_source.why: An annual energy target was asked for on a series read from a snapshot window, whose year outside the window is unknown. The detail asks for the window's MWh; the assistant restates it with basis window, per call.

measured_series_kept.why: A default series was about to replace a component that carries a measured upload (one arrived after the preview). The row is skipped and says so; the others apply. The assistant reports the row, per call.

point_not_in_profile.why: apply_generated_profile asked for a point the pending profile does not hold. The detail lists the points it does hold; the assistant picks the right point_id, per call.

no_points.why: A profile preview or generation named no sites: neither points nor from_generators. The assistant asks which generators or coordinates to use, per call.

unknown_generator.why: from_generators named a generator the open network does not hold. The detail lists the names not found; the assistant lists the candidates and asks again, per call.

missing_coordinates.why: from_generators named generators whose bus has no usable coordinates (unset, out of range, or the 0/0 default). The detail lists them; the assistant offers both remedies per call: set the bus coordinates (an edit with its own card) or upload a profile.

unreachable_target.why: A shaping op asked for full-load hours or a capacity factor beyond what the profile can reach by scaling with clip-at-1. The detail names the reachable maximum; the assistant proposes a reachable target or another weather year/preset, per call.

malformed_job_id.why: A pending-profile job id that would escape the project's pending folder. Only a mistyped or forged id reaches this; the assistant lists the pending profiles and uses one of their ids.

unknown_grid_code_profile.why: campus_grid_readiness was asked for a grid-code profile that is neither shipped nor published in the project. The detail lists the known ones; the assistant picks one of them or asks the user. There is no conversation-wide recovery action.

continuation_unavailable.why: LC-12: a continuation turn named a job with no continuation due to this session (none finished, already continued, the plan was cancelled, the job was aborted, or another session or project). The turn does not start and nothing runs; the panel simply stops offering it.

plan_continue_unavailable.why: LC-23 COP-1: the user's Continue on the plan card named a plan that is not paused at a card (already continued, cancelled, or another project), or the request also carried a message. The turn does not start and nothing runs; the plan card stops offering Continue.

invalid_continuation.why: LC-12: /stream carried continuation_job_id together with typed words, attachments, a script or checked fields. A continuation is written by the harness, never by the user; the request is refused before any turn.

task_step_out_of_order.why: LC-05: a plan step was called before an earlier step completed (for example the run after a refused edit). Refused before any card or job; the detail names the step it waits on, and the assistant says which earlier step failed and why.

task_step_waiting.why: LC-12: the plan step is already waiting on its job, so it never runs twice. Refused before any card; the conversation continues when the job ends.

snapshot_manifest_unknown.why: restore_project_snapshot: the snapshot's capture_manifest.json has a version this build does not know (taken by a newer app), so the restore is refused before anything changes. The model says so; restoring needs that newer version or a different snapshot.

changed_during_restore.why: restore_project_snapshot: an edit landed between the pre-restore save and the restore's lock, so nothing was restored (it would be in neither the before-restore snapshot nor the restored state). The model says so and offers to retry within the turn.

dc_load_invalid.why: create_project_from_template on a data center with a dc_load the template refuses (a phase off the investment periods, a peak above the energized import plus firm gensets; DC-01). The detail names the field; the model corrects the argument and retries, like invalid_tool_args. Nothing is created.

planning_invalid.why: create_project_from_template on a staged example with a planning entry it refuses (a year out of range, dates not increasing, start equal to end, or a build that fails the template rules; E1). The detail names the field; the model corrects the years and retries. Nothing is created.

template_params_invalid.why: create_project_from_template with a body key the template does not take (planning on a template without staged years, dc_load off a data center). The detail names the key; the model drops it and retries. Nothing is created.

table_too_large.why: preview_equipment_mapping / apply_equipment_mapping (data-to-model slice 1) refused a table over 500 data rows, 40 columns or 200 characters in a cell instead of truncating it. `limits` names the bound; the assistant asks the user to split the file, per call.

table_unsafe.why: preview_equipment_mapping / apply_equipment_mapping (data-to-model slice 1) refused an XLSX before parsing it: it inflates past 100 MiB or 100x compression, or an XML part declares a DOCTYPE or entity. The assistant says the workbook cannot be read and asks for a plain re-save or a CSV, per call.

unreadable_table.why: preview_equipment_mapping / apply_equipment_mapping (data-to-model slice 1) could not read the upload as a table (not UTF-8 CSV, not an XLSX zip, empty sheet). The detail says which; the assistant asks for a readable file, per call.

sheet_not_found.why: preview_equipment_mapping / apply_equipment_mapping (data-to-model slice 1) was given a sheet the workbook does not have. The detail lists `sheets`; the assistant retries with one of them or asks the user which, per call.

source_changed.why: preview_equipment_mapping / apply_equipment_mapping (data-to-model slice 1) found the upload's bytes differ from the previewed sha256 (or from the upload's own recorded digest). Nothing was written; the assistant previews the table again, per call.

unsupported_table_format.why: preview_equipment_mapping / apply_equipment_mapping (data-to-model slice 1) was pointed at an upload that is not a CSV or XLSX. The assistant asks for a table file or uses the import that fits the upload, per call.

duplicate_header.why: preview_equipment_mapping / apply_equipment_mapping (data-to-model slice 1) refused a table with two columns under one header, since a mapping names columns by header. The detail names the header; the assistant asks the user to rename one, per call.

column_not_found.why: preview_equipment_mapping / apply_equipment_mapping (data-to-model slice 1) was given a name_column or mapped column the table does not have. The detail lists the headers; the assistant retries with an exact header, per call.

empty_mapping.why: preview_equipment_mapping / apply_equipment_mapping (data-to-model slice 1) was called with no column mapped onto a field. The assistant maps at least one column (fields from get_component_schema) and calls again, per call.

mapping_too_large.why: preview_equipment_mapping / apply_equipment_mapping (data-to-model slice 1) would show more than 200 changed cells on one card. `limits` names the bound; the assistant maps fewer rows or columns per apply, per call.

table_confirmation_needed.why: preview_equipment_mapping / apply_equipment_mapping (data-to-model slice 1) needs a confirmation the user has not given (`missing`, e.g. money_year when the table's money year differs from the investment case's). The assistant asks the user, then calls again with confirm=[...], per call.

nothing_to_change.why: preview_equipment_mapping / apply_equipment_mapping (data-to-model slice 1) found every mapped value already equal to the network's (a repeat apply). Nothing was written and no card was shown; the assistant tells the user, per call.

edit_preview_stale.why: apply_equipment_mapping refused because the network moved between the card the user approved and the live write (another edit, or a different digest on the HTTP apply). Nothing was written; the assistant proposes the edit again, per call.

batch_refused.why: apply_generated_profiles found members that cannot be applied (carrier mismatch, a point the job lacks, an unaligned series). Nothing was written; the detail names every bad member and the assistant reports them, per call.

duplicate_member.why: apply_generated_profiles listed one component twice. It appears in the batch_refused member list; the assistant drops the repeat and retries.

no_members.why: apply_generated_profiles had no members: none named, or all_from_job found no point named after a wind/solar generator. The detail lists the job's points; the assistant names the components or says nothing fits.

batch_partially_applied.why: A write failed midway through apply_generated_profiles. The detail names what was and was not applied; the assistant says so and that one Undo reverts the whole batch.
